cause: Plasmodium parasites
transmission: Mainly bites of infected female Anopheles mosquitoes
common_symptoms: Fever, chills, headache; severe disease can cause confusion, seizures and difficulty breathing
prevention: Avoid mosquito bites; use recommended preventive medicines when appropriate; early testing
medical_note: Suspected malaria should be confirmed with parasite-based testing and treated promptly

cause: Mycobacterium tuberculosis bacteria
transmission: Airborne spread from people with TB, especially through coughing, sneezing or spitting
common_symptoms: Prolonged cough, chest pain, weakness, fatigue, weight loss, fever, night sweats
prevention: Early detection and treatment; vaccination in countries where BCG is recommended; reduce exposure and improve ventilation
medical_note: TB is preventable and curable; treatment requires prescribed antibiotics and adherence

cause: Insufficient insulin production or ineffective use of insulin
transmission: Not contagious
common_symptoms: Increased thirst, frequent urination, blurred vision, tiredness, unintentional weight loss
prevention: Healthy diet, regular physical activity, healthy body weight and avoiding tobacco can help prevent or delay type 2 diabetes
medical_note: Diagnosis and treatment require healthcare assessment; management may include lifestyle measures, medicines and monitoring

cause: Airway inflammation and narrowing; triggers vary between people
transmission: Not contagious
common_symptoms: Cough, wheezing, shortness of breath, chest tightness
prevention: Identify and reduce personal triggers; follow an individualized asthma management plan
medical_note: Inhaled medicines can control symptoms; diagnosis and treatment should be guided by a healthcare professional

cause: Rabies virus
transmission: Usually saliva from an infected animal through bites or scratches
common_symptoms: Once clinical symptoms appear, rabies causes severe neurological disease and is virtually 100% fatal
prevention: Vaccinate dogs; avoid animal bites; immediately wash wounds and seek post-exposure care after a potentially risky exposure
medical_note: Prompt post-exposure prophylaxis can prevent disease after exposure; seek medical care immediately

cause: Dengue virus
transmission: Bites of infected Aedes mosquitoes
common_symptoms: High fever, headache, pain behind the eyes, muscle/joint pain, nausea, vomiting, rash
prevention: Avoid mosquito bites, especially during the day; reduce mosquito breeding sites
medical_note: There is no specific antiviral treatment; severe symptoms require immediate medical care

cause: Persistently high blood pressure; multiple genetic, environmental and lifestyle factors can contribute
transmission: Not contagious
common_symptoms: Often no symptoms; very high blood pressure may cause severe headache, chest pain, dizziness, breathing difficulty or vision changes
prevention: Healthy diet, physical activity, reducing salt, avoiding tobacco and managing risk factors; regular blood-pressure checks
medical_note: Blood pressure measurement is needed for detection; very high blood pressure with concerning symptoms needs immediate care

cause: Interruption of brain blood flow due to blockage or bleeding
transmission: Not contagious
common_symptoms: Sudden facial droop, arm weakness, speech difficulty, vision loss, dizziness or loss of balance
prevention: Control blood pressure, avoid tobacco, maintain a healthy diet and physical activity, and manage other risk factors
medical_note: Stroke is a medical emergency; rapid assessment and treatment are essential

cause: Vibrio cholerae bacteria
transmission: Food or water contaminated with the bacterium
common_symptoms: Acute watery diarrhoea and dehydration; severe illness can progress rapidly
prevention: Safe drinking water, sanitation, hygiene and vaccination where recommended
medical_note: Rapid rehydration is critical; severe cases may require intravenous fluids and other medical treatment

cause: SARS-CoV-2 coronavirus
transmission: Mainly through infectious respiratory particles, especially in close contact or shared indoor spaces
common_symptoms: Fever, chills, sore throat; other symptoms can occur
prevention: Follow current vaccination recommendations and reduce exposure to infectious respiratory particles
medical_note: Most people recover without treatment, but people at higher risk of severe disease should seek medical advice promptly

cause: Hepatitis B virus (HBV)
transmission: Mother-to-child during birth; blood and certain body-fluid exposures, including sexual transmission
common_symptoms: May be asymptomatic; acute infection can cause illness and chronic infection can damage the liver
prevention: Hepatitis B vaccination; safe injection practices and prevention of blood/body-fluid exposure
medical_note: Chronic infection can lead to cirrhosis and liver cancer; medical evaluation is important

cause: Salmonella Typhi bacteria
transmission: Usually contaminated food or water
common_symptoms: Prolonged fever, fatigue, headache, nausea, abdominal pain, constipation or diarrhoea; sometimes rash
prevention: Safe water, sanitation, hand hygiene and typhoid vaccination where recommended
medical_note: Can be treated with antibiotics, but resistance can complicate treatment; diagnosis should be medically confirmed

cause: Long-term lung damage; tobacco smoke and household air pollution are important risk factors
transmission: Not contagious
common_symptoms: Persistent cough, sometimes with phlegm, difficulty breathing, wheezing and tiredness
prevention: Avoid tobacco smoke and reduce exposure to household and environmental air pollution
medical_note: Symptoms can be managed with medical treatment and risk-factor reduction; diagnosis requires clinical assessment

cause: Influenza viruses (Type A and B)
transmission: Airborne droplets and contact with contaminated surfaces
common_symptoms: Sudden high fever, body aches, chills, dry cough, sore throat, fatigue
prevention: Annual influenza vaccination, hand hygiene
medical_note: Antivirals such as oseltamivir may shorten illness when prescribed and started early

cause: Viruses, most commonly rhinoviruses
transmission: Direct contact or airborne droplets from sneezes and coughs
common_symptoms: Runny nose, sore throat, cough, congestion, mild headache, sneezing
prevention: Frequent hand washing and avoiding face touching
medical_note: Usually self-limiting; antibiotics are ineffective against viral colds

cause: Bacterial, viral, or fungal infections
transmission: Inhalation of airborne droplets or respiratory spread
common_symptoms: Cough with phlegm, fever, chills, difficulty breathing, sharp chest pain
prevention: Pneumococcal and influenza vaccination and smoking cessation
medical_note: Clinical assessment and appropriate testing are needed to determine the cause
source: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)

cause: Viral infections or exposure to smoke and air pollutants
transmission: Airborne droplets and direct contact
common_symptoms: Hacking cough producing mucus, fatigue, shortness of breath
prevention: Avoid smoking and follow recommended influenza and pneumonia vaccination
medical_note: Acute bronchitis often resolves in weeks; chronic symptoms require medical evaluation

cause: Bordetella pertussis bacteria
transmission: Airborne respiratory droplets
common_symptoms: Severe hacking cough with a whooping sound, runny nose, mild fever
prevention: DTaP and Tdap vaccination series
medical_note: It can be dangerous for infants; early medical assessment is important
source: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)

cause: Insulin resistance or inadequate insulin production
transmission: Non-communicable; genetics obesity inactivity and diet can contribute
common_symptoms: Excessive thirst, frequent urination, unexplained weight loss, fatigue
prevention: Balanced high-fiber diet, regular exercise, and weight management
medical_note: Monitoring may include fasting blood glucose and HbA1c testing

cause: Autoimmune destruction of insulin-producing pancreatic cells
transmission: Non-communicable; genetic and environmental factors can contribute
common_symptoms: Extreme thirst, frequent urination, constant hunger, sudden weight loss
prevention: There is no known primary prevention currently available
medical_note: Treatment requires healthcare assessment and prescribed insulin
source: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)

cause: Caloric intake exceeding energy expenditure over time
transmission: Non-communicable; dietary habits sedentary lifestyle and genetics can contribute
common_symptoms: Excess body fat, joint strain, breathlessness, fatigue
prevention: Nutritious balanced diet and regular physical activity
medical_note: It is a major risk factor for cardiovascular disease and diabetes; assessment should be individualized

cause: Accumulation of uric acid crystals in joints
transmission: Non-communicable; diet alcohol and genetics can contribute
common_symptoms: Intense joint pain, swelling, redness, and lingering discomfort
prevention: Limit alcohol and purine-rich foods and maintain hydration
medical_note: Treatment should be guided by a healthcare professional

cause: Atherosclerosis narrowing the coronary arteries
transmission: Non-communicable; genetics cholesterol smoking and hypertension can contribute
common_symptoms: Chest pain, shortness of breath, fatigue, palpitations
prevention: Heart-healthy diet, exercise, and quitting smoking
medical_note: It can lead to a heart attack; chest pain with emergency symptoms requires urgent care

cause: Inability of the heart to pump blood efficiently due to damage
transmission: Non-communicable; coronary disease hypertension and diabetes can contribute
common_symptoms: Shortness of breath, fatigue, swelling in legs and ankles
prevention: Control blood pressure and diabetes and follow individualized sodium guidance
medical_note: Management requires prescribed treatment and regular clinical follow-up
source: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)

cause: Dengue virus transmitted by Aedes mosquitoes
transmission: Vector-borne through mosquito bites; not usually person-to-person
common_symptoms: High fever, severe headache, eye pain, joint or muscle pain, rash
prevention: Use insect repellent, remove standing water, and use window screens
medical_note: Seek medical advice; aspirin and ibuprofen may be unsafe when bleeding risk is present

cause: Chikungunya virus carried by Aedes mosquitoes
transmission: Vector-borne through mosquito bites
common_symptoms: Sudden fever, severe joint pain, muscle pain, headache
prevention: Prevent mosquito bites and remove standing water
medical_note: Joint pain can persist; medical assessment is advised for severe or persistent symptoms
source: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)

cause: Zika virus spread by Aedes mosquitoes
transmission: Vector-borne, sexual transmission, and mother-to-fetus transmission
common_symptoms: Mild fever, rash, conjunctivitis, muscle and joint pain
prevention: Use mosquito repellent, practice safer sex, and follow travel precautions
medical_note: Infection during pregnancy can harm the developing fetus; seek medical advice promptly

cause: Yellow fever virus transmitted by mosquitoes
transmission: Vector-borne through infected mosquito bites
common_symptoms: Fever, muscle pain, headache, loss of appetite, jaundice
prevention: Yellow fever vaccination where recommended and bite protection
medical_note: Severe illness can affect the liver and kidneys and requires urgent care

cause: Salmonella Typhi bacteria
transmission: Ingestion of food or water contaminated by feces
common_symptoms: Prolonged high fever, headache, stomach pain, constipation or diarrhea
prevention: Typhoid vaccination, safe water, and thorough cooking
medical_note: Treatment requires medical assessment and prescribed antibiotics
source: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)

cause: Hepatitis A virus infecting liver cells
transmission: Fecal-oral route through contaminated food water or close contact
common_symptoms: Fatigue, nausea, abdominal pain, dark urine, jaundice
prevention: Hepatitis A vaccination, safe drinking water, and hand hygiene
medical_note: Medical evaluation is recommended for jaundice or severe symptoms
source: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)

cause: Viral or bacterial pathogens
transmission: Fecal-oral route contaminated food or direct contact
common_symptoms: Watery diarrhea, abdominal cramps, nausea, vomiting, low fever
prevention: Hand hygiene, safe food preparation, and recommended vaccination
medical_note: Preventing dehydration with oral rehydration is important; severe dehydration needs urgent care
source: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)

cause: Human Immunodeficiency Virus targeting immune CD4 T cells
transmission: Sexual contact, contaminated needles, blood, and mother-to-child transmission
common_symptoms: Flu-like illness early on, weight loss, recurrent fevers later
prevention: PrEP when appropriate, consistent condom use, and safe needle practices
medical_note: Antiretroviral treatment suppresses the virus; testing and clinical care are essential

cause: Hepatitis C virus
transmission: Direct contact with infected blood
common_symptoms: Often asymptomatic for years; fatigue, nausea, jaundice
prevention: Avoid sharing needles and use sterile medical equipment
medical_note: Direct-acting antivirals can cure many infections under medical supervision

cause: Treponema pallidum bacteria
transmission: Direct contact with a syphilis sore during sexual activity
common_symptoms: Painless sores, non-itchy rashes, and possible later neurological effects
prevention: Condom use, regular STI screening, and partner treatment
medical_note: It is treatable; prompt testing and prescribed treatment are important
source: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)

cause: Neisseria gonorrhoeae bacteria
transmission: Sexual contact with an infected partner
common_symptoms: Painful urination, abnormal genital discharge, lower abdominal pain
prevention: Condom use and routine STI testing
medical_note: Antibiotic resistance is increasing; treatment must be prescribed
source: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)

cause: Chlamydia trachomatis bacteria
transmission: Unprotected sexual contact
common_symptoms: Often asymptomatic; painful urination, unusual discharge, pelvic inflammatory disease
prevention: Condom use and routine annual screening
medical_note: Testing and prescribed antibiotics are needed; partners may also need treatment
source: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)

cause: Underactive thyroid producing insufficient hormones
transmission: Non-communicable; autoimmune disease iodine deficiency and genetics can contribute
common_symptoms: Fatigue, weight gain, cold intolerance, dry skin, constipation
prevention: Adequate iodine intake and monitoring when clinically indicated
medical_note: Treatment requires medical assessment and prescribed thyroid hormone

cause: Overactive thyroid producing excess hormones
transmission: Non-communicable; autoimmune disease and thyroid nodules can contribute
common_symptoms: Weight loss, rapid heartbeat, anxiety, tremors, heat intolerance
prevention: Avoid excess iodine and seek assessment for persistent symptoms
medical_note: Treatment may include prescribed medicines or other specialist care

cause: Decrease in bone mineral density and mass
transmission: Non-communicable; aging menopause and nutrient deficiency can contribute
common_symptoms: Often silent until fracture; height loss or stooped posture
prevention: Adequate calcium and vitamin D and weight-bearing exercise
medical_note: Diagnosis may require bone-density testing

cause: Gradual loss of kidney function over time
transmission: Non-communicable; diabetes hypertension and kidney disease can contribute
common_symptoms: Fatigue, ankle swelling, persistent itching, urination changes
prevention: Control blood sugar and blood pressure and follow medical hydration advice
medical_note: Evaluation may include eGFR and urine albumin testing
source: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)

cause: Mineral and salt deposits forming inside the kidneys
transmission: Non-communicable; dehydration sodium intake and other factors can contribute
common_symptoms: Severe flank pain, blood in urine, cloudy urine, nausea
prevention: Drink adequate water and reduce dietary sodium as advised
medical_note: Large or obstructing stones need medical treatment

cause: Bacterial infection entering the urinary tract
transmission: Usually not spread between people; bacteria can enter through the urethra
common_symptoms: Strong urge to urinate, burning, cloudy or strong-smelling urine
prevention: Hydration, appropriate hygiene, and urinating after intercourse
medical_note: Testing and prescribed antibiotics may be needed
source: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)

cause: Accumulation of excess fat in liver cells
transmission: Non-communicable; obesity type 2 diabetes and metabolic syndrome can contribute
common_symptoms: Often silent; fatigue or upper right abdominal discomfort
prevention: Healthy weight, balanced diet, exercise, and limiting added sugar
medical_note: It can progress to liver inflammation or scarring and needs medical evaluation

cause: Sores on the stomach or intestinal lining caused by H. pylori or NSAIDs
transmission: Usually non-communicable; H. pylori can spread through contaminated food or water
common_symptoms: Burning stomach pain, bloating, heartburn
prevention: Hand hygiene and avoiding chronic overuse of NSAIDs
medical_note: Testing and prescribed treatment are needed

cause: Immune reaction to dietary gluten
transmission: Non-communicable; genetic predisposition can contribute
common_symptoms: Chronic diarrhea, bloating, fatigue, weight loss, anemia
prevention: There is no primary prevention; confirmed cases require a strict gluten-free diet
medical_note: Medical testing is needed before changing diet for diagnosis

cause: Disorder affecting bowel function and brain-gut interaction
transmission: Non-communicable; stress food sensitivities and other factors can contribute
common_symptoms: Abdominal cramping, pain, bloating, diarrhea or constipation
prevention: Stress management, identifying triggers, and individualized dietary guidance
medical_note: Diagnosis requires clinical assessment to exclude other causes

cause: Clouding of the eye lens due to protein changes over time
transmission: Non-communicable; aging UV exposure diabetes and smoking can contribute
common_symptoms: Cloudy vision, faded colors, nighttime glare
prevention: UV-blocking sunglasses, smoking cessation, and blood-sugar management
medical_note: Vision changes require an eye examination

cause: Optic nerve damage associated with high intraocular pressure
transmission: Non-communicable; genetics age and eye pressure can contribute
common_symptoms: Gradual loss of peripheral vision or tunnel vision
prevention: Regular comprehensive eye examinations
medical_note: Lost vision cannot be recovered, so early assessment is important

cause: Brain-cell degeneration involving amyloid plaques and tau changes
transmission: Non-communicable; age genetics and cardiovascular health can contribute
common_symptoms: Memory loss, confusion, difficulty solving problems, mood changes
prevention: Mental stimulation, regular exercise, and healthy diet
medical_note: Evaluation and ongoing support should be guided by healthcare professionals

cause: Abnormal brain activity affecting nerve signals and blood vessels
transmission: Non-communicable; genetics hormones stress and diet can contribute
common_symptoms: Throbbing headache, nausea, and light or sound sensitivity
prevention: Avoid personal triggers and maintain regular sleep and eating patterns
medical_note: Persistent or severe headaches need medical assessment

cause: Disorder involving abnormal electrical activity in the brain
transmission: Non-communicable; genetics trauma stroke and infections can contribute
common_symptoms: Temporary confusion, staring spells, stiff muscles, seizures
prevention: Prevent head injuries and follow prescribed treatment
medical_note: Seizures require medical assessment and safety planning

cause: Interaction of social psychological and biological factors
transmission: Non-communicable; genetics brain chemistry and life stressors can contribute
common_symptoms: Persistent sadness, loss of interest, fatigue, sleep problems
prevention: Stress management, social support, and early professional help
medical_note: Treatment may include psychotherapy and prescribed medication

cause: Inadequate iron intake blood loss or reduced absorption
transmission: Non-communicable; dietary and physiological factors can contribute
common_symptoms: Fatigue, weakness, pale skin, shortness of breath, dizziness
prevention: Iron-rich foods paired with vitamin C when appropriate
medical_note: Confirmation requires blood testing and medical evaluation

cause: Severe vitamin C deficiency
transmission: Non-communicable; inadequate intake of fresh produce can contribute
common_symptoms: Fatigue, bleeding gums, bruising, joint pain
prevention: Consume vitamin-C-rich foods such as citrus fruits berries and vegetables
medical_note: Medical advice is recommended for suspected deficiency

cause: Autoimmune attack on the joint lining
transmission: Non-communicable; genetics hormones and smoking can contribute
common_symptoms: Tender swollen joints, symmetrical involvement, morning stiffness
prevention: Smoking cessation and early medical assessment
medical_note: Prescribed disease-modifying treatment can prevent joint damage

cause: Autoimmune condition causing rapid skin-cell growth
transmission: Non-communicable; genetics immune factors and stress can contribute
common_symptoms: Raised scaly patches, dry cracked skin, itching
prevention: Avoid skin trauma, manage stress, and avoid smoking
medical_note: Treatment should be guided by a healthcare professional
